claims.claim: Human oral bioavailability measurements for lipophilic carboxylic acids relevant to the query are all above the 20% threshold: palmitic acid 28% (C16), oxybate about 25-30% (C05, C13, C18), and neotame at least 34.3% (C20).
Complex lipophilic drugs with moderate oral absorption, lefamulin (25-25.8% fasted) and eplerenone (69-98%), indicate that the query's size and lipophilicity do not preclude F >=20%.
No visible L1 record provides an affirmative low (<20%) oral-bioavailability outcome for a transferable context; the low physicochemical prior is explicitly not endpoint proof.

evidence_gaps: No direct oral bioavailability measurement for the query molecule itself.
Reference contexts are not exact structural matches; formulation, dose, and first-pass metabolism may differ.
Oxybate records conflict (about 25-30% vs 88%), adding uncertainty to the acid-transfer analogy.
The query's hemiacetal, ketone, and gem-difluoride may confer unique metabolism not represented in the visible records.
The low physicochemical prior is not endpoint proof and is insufficient alone to affirm F <20%.
content.decision_summary: Predicted high because all transferable L1 human oral-bioavailability records for lipophilic carboxylic acids and complex lipophilic drugs are at or above 24-28%, exceeding the 20% threshold; the low physicochemical prior is insufficient to affirm F <20% without direct low-outcome evidence.
